citation: Anoop S, et al. Lipid accumulation product (LAP) as a potential index to predict risk of insulin resistance in young, non-obese Asian Indian males from Southern India: observations from hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp studies. BMJ Open Diabetes Res Care 2021;9:e002414.
protocol: Hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp (2 h), insulin infusion printed as 40 mU/kg/min (elsewhere in the text cited as 40 mU/m2), dextrose varied to hold plasma glucose 90 mg/dl (5 mmol/L); M value from 60-120 min.
population: 108 young normoglycaemic non-obese Asian Indian men, age 19.7 +/- 1 y, BMI 19.1 +/- 2.5 (Vellore birth cohort).
note: Largest clamp sample here and South Asian. The insulin infusion unit is inconsistent in the text (mU/kg/min versus mU/m2), and the postprandial point is a single undefined sample, so treat that cautiously; skewed variables are medians marked with an asterisk.
